Task Guide:

Simulate the fracture behavior of a Σ3(111) symmetric tilt grain boundary (STGB) in body-centered cubic (BCC) iron using LAMMPS. The simulation should begin by reading a pre-generated grain boundary structure file (present at /structures/task_9/Fe_110_sig3.txt) that defines a bicrystal with a tilt direction of <110> and a grain boundary plane of <111>. The simulation should use metal units and atome_style atomic, and box should have periodic boundary conditions in all directions. After initialization, perform an energy minimization using the conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm with force and energy tolerances of 1.0e-15 and a maximum of 1000 iterations and use the EAM potential present at (/potentials/EAM/Fe-C_Hepburn_Ackland.eam.fs). The box should be allowed to relax along the x and z directions while maintaining a fixed y-direction. Following minimization, apply uniaxial tensile loading perpendicular to the grain boundary (y-direction). Atoms far from the boundary should be deleted to avoid artifacts, and atoms at the edges should be fixed before the deformation begins. The strain should be applied in increments, with the fixed groups being displaced incrementally, followed by energy minimization at each step. During the simulation, compute the stress tensor components and store stress-strain data in a text file called stress_strain.txt. The file should contain strain values and stress components converted from bars to GPa in the format strain,stress_xx,stress_yy,stress_zz without any column names or metadata. As the final result, report the maximum tensile stress (in GPa) along the x-direction achieved prior to the onset of plastic deformation or structural instability, identified as the first significant drop in the stress-strain response. Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/comprehensive/task_9/task_9_trial_1 directory. You can use the available I/O tools (e.g., write_file) make new files .etc. Whatever potentials you need to run the simulation, you can find them at /potentials/. A type of potential can be accessed by /potentials/TYPE where TYPE can be [EAM, TERSOFF, REAXFF] which further contains the exact potential files. Note that in case of reaxff potentials, pair style 'reax/c' has been renamed to 'reaxff' and always use NULL for the control file (cfile), for example, this syntax is correct : pair_style reaxff NULL. If the task is to give the final output as a scalar, only return the numerical value, without any units.

{"path": "/results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/comprehensive/task_9/task_9_trial_1/gb_tension.in", "content": "# LAMMPS input script for Fe grain boundary tension simulation
units metal
atom_style atomic
boundary p p p

# Read structure
read_data /structures/task_9/Fe_110_sig3.txt

# Define potential
pair_style eam/fs
pair_coeff * * /potentials/EAM/Fe-C_Hepburn_Ackland.eam.fs Fe

# Energy minimization
fix box_relax all box/relax x 0 z 0
minimize 1.0e-15 1.0e-15 1000 1000
unfix box_relax

# Define groups for fixed regions
group top region top
group bottom region bottom
group mobile subtract all top bottom

# Set up output
variable strain equal "(ly - v_L0)/v_L0"
variable stress_xx equal "pxx*0.0001"  # Convert from bars to GPa
variable stress_yy equal "pyy*0.0001"
variable stress_zz equal "pzz*0.0001"

# Initialize variables
variable L0 equal ly
variable strain_rate equal 0.001
variable N_steps equal 1000
variable delta_strain equal ${strain_rate}/${N_steps}

# Output file
fix output all print 10 "${strain} ${stress_xx} ${stress_yy} ${stress_zz}" file stress_strain.txt screen no

# Deformation loop
label loop
variable i loop ${N_steps}
    # Increment strain
    displace_atoms top move 0.0 ${delta_strain} 0.0
    displace_atoms bottom move 0.0 -${delta_strain} 0.0
    
    # Minimize at each step
    minimize 1.0e-15 1.0e-15 1000 1000
    
next i
jump SELF loop

# End simulation
write_dump all custom dump.lammpstrj id type x y z"}
